name: Pelvar Black Sesame-Caramel Coins
description: Thin pressed discs of synth-caramel layered with roasted black sesame paste, finished with a matte cocoa-substitute shell that snaps cleanly. Sold in foil rolls of eight.
flavor_profile: Nutty, slightly bitter black sesame balanced against rich caramel sweetness, with a faintly smoky finish from the cocoa-sub shell
cultural_context: Pelvar Coins are considered a 'grown-up' candy — gifted between coworkers, shared at the end of meetings, or used as a low-stakes gesture of goodwill. In Tier 2 workplaces, leaving a foil roll on someone's desk is a recognized social signal that you want to clear the air after a conflict.
story_hooks: A Halvex executive has been using Pelvar Coin distributions as a cover for passing physical dead-drop messages within their corponation — the foil wrapping contains micro-printed data visible only under certain wavelengths.

A street confectioner claims the original Pelvar Black Sesame formula was stolen from her grandmother's recipe by a Halvex talent scout in the 2160s — she has documentation and wants help pursuing it.

The cocoa-substitute shell supplier has quietly switched to a compound with trace mood-modulating properties; Pelvar's quality assurance team has noticed anomalous user behavior data but hasn't gone public.
related_entities: Carrion Defense Works Entropic Shotgun ES-4 'Ragnarok'
